verdict: The live plumbing is solid: coalesced deltas, hibernation-safe snapshots, completions de-duplicated and batched. The surface itself only shows the happy path - a session whose socket drops or that ends in errors vanishes instead of being surfaced, 'dismiss' does not stick, and 'Finished this hour' can show sessions from yesterday.

findings.title: Show stalled and disconnected sessions instead of hiding them
findings.scenario: An uploader's tab crashes or loses network mid-transfer; webSocketClose marks the session 'stale', and renderLive() filters to state === 'uploading'.
findings.consequence: The one session the admin most needs to see - someone whose upload died at 60% - disappears from the Live tab at once, never appears under 'Finished this hour', and is pruned from the DO two minutes later with no trace on this surface.
findings.fix: Render sessions with state 'stale' or 'error' in a 'Stopped' group below the active list (reusing makeLiveRow with a muted class and 'last seen Xs ago'), and on prune() push a summary with outcome 'stopped' into recentDone the same way noteFinished() does.

findings.title: Make 'dismiss' stick, or remove it
findings.scenario: Admin clicks 'dismiss' on a session that is still uploading.
findings.consequence: /close deletes the session, but the uploader's next progress frame (~1.2 s later) goes through recordSession() and recreates it, so the card reappears; the button looks broken.
findings.fix: Keep a `dismissed` Map of session id -> expiry (e.g. 10 min) in the DO; /close adds to it and recordProgress() returns early for dismissed ids (still feeding digests). Alternatively label the button 'hide' and keep the hidden ids client-side only.

findings.title: Write stats before the recent list so a failed flush cannot drop counts
findings.scenario: The recent:<slug> put succeeds but the stats:<slug> put throws (KV write limit, transient error); flush() requeues the batch.
findings.consequence: On retry every file id is already in recent:<slug>, newFiles is 0, and flushOne returns before touching stats - those files and bytes are permanently missing from the link's counters and the day rollup.
findings.fix: Compute newFiles/newBytes, put stats:<slug> and bumpDay first, then put recent:<slug>; a retry after a failed recent put then at worst re-adds rows that mergeRecent de-duplicates.

findings.title: Apply the one-hour cutoff when recentDone is read, not only when a session finishes
findings.scenario: The last upload finished yesterday afternoon and nothing has finished since.
findings.consequence: 'Finished this hour' still lists yesterday's sessions, and 'Last completed' reads like it just happened.
findings.fix: Filter recentDone by endedAt >= now - 3600_000 in /snapshot, the admin-socket snapshot and wake(); client-side, filter liveRecent the same way in renderLive().

findings.title: Stop re-rendering every live card once a second
findings.scenario: A keyboard or screen-reader admin tabs to the 'dismiss' or 'Drive folder' button on a live card.
findings.consequence: tickLive() calls updateLiveRow(), which replaces the card's innerHTML every second even when nothing changed, so focus and hover are lost and the button can be swapped out between mousedown and click.
findings.fix: Drop the 1 s tickLive re-render (nothing in the cards is time-relative) and render only on socket messages; or in updateLiveRow compare a cheap signature (pct, sent, state, files length) against el._sig before writing innerHTML.

missing_features.title: Stopped / failed sessions group
missing_features.why: An uploader messages 'it stopped working' - the admin needs to see which session died, at which file, and when.
missing_features.where: Live tab, under the active list
missing_features.depends_on: already available (sessions with state 'stale' live in the DO for 2 min; telemetry has the error events)

missing_features.title: Per-file error reason on the live card
missing_features.why: A file row turns red with no reason; the error code (E_STALL, E_QUOTA...) is already in the client taxonomy.
missing_features.depends_on: progress frames would need to carry file.error

interlinks.to: Link detail upload-session log for that session id
interlinks.why: goes straight from 'someone finished' to what they sent

interlinks.from: Uploader name/avatar on a live card
interlinks.why: tells the admin who this is and what they sent before

interlinks.to: the uploader's own subfolder, not the link root
interlinks.why: the root folder holds every uploader's files

layout: Order the Live tab as: active sessions, stopped sessions, finished this hour - the current empty-state card duplicates 'Last completed' and the finished list when both are visible.
